title: Synthetic Sighting Generator and Ground-Truth Scenario Framework
objective: Generate realistic synthetic sighting data with known ground truth, so that the matching and path-reconstruction engines (stages 6-8) can be developed and measured precisely before any real video or CV model is involved.
context_for_agent: This is the highest-leverage stage in the project. With a ground-truth generator you can measure precision and recall of the matching engine directly, tune thresholds empirically, and catch regressions — none of which is possible if you go straight to real footage where you never truly know the right answer. Model the failure modes of real ALPR faithfully: that realism is the entire point.

tasks.name: Scenario specification format
tasks.detail: Define a Scenario model describing a synthetic dataset: topology reference, time span, list of VehicleSpec entries (plate, object_class, a route as an ordered list of camera_ids, departure time, speed profile), a background traffic specification (volume of decoy vehicles), and a noise profile reference. Scenarios are declarative and serializable to YAML so they can be committed and reused as regression fixtures.

tasks.name: Route simulation
tasks.detail: Given a route through the topology, generate sightings with timestamps derived from the actual CameraLink travel-time windows plus configurable jitter. Sightings must be topology-consistent by construction (this produces the 'correct answer'). Support routes that revisit a camera, routes that skip covered cameras (simulating a missed detection), and routes that leave and re-enter the covered area.

tasks.name: Plate OCR noise model
tasks.detail: Implement a configurable noise model that corrupts plate readings realistically: (a) ambiguity substitutions weighted by real-world confusion frequency (O/0, I/1/L, S/5, B/8, Z/2, G/6); (b) character dropout (plate partially occluded, producing a shorter string); (c) complete read failure producing plate_text=None with an embedding still present; (d) spurious extra characters from frame borders or bumper stickers; (e) confidence values correlated with corruption severity so that low-quality reads carry low confidence, as real OCR does. Each corruption event is recorded in ground truth so tests can assert on specific failure modes.

tasks.name: Embedding simulation
tasks.detail: Generate synthetic re-id embeddings with controllable intra-vehicle and inter-vehicle similarity: each vehicle has a base vector; each sighting's embedding is the base plus Gaussian noise scaled by a configurable intra_class_sigma, then L2-normalized. Decoy vehicles are drawn to produce a configurable inter_class_similarity distribution, including a 'hard negatives' option generating decoys deliberately close to the target (simulating same make/model/color vehicles). Without hard negatives the matching engine will look far better than it is.

tasks.name: Background traffic generation
tasks.detail: Generate decoy vehicles traversing plausible topology routes at a configurable volume, so the target is a needle in a realistic haystack. Decoy plates are drawn from a generator that can produce plates within a configurable edit distance of the target plate, to stress fuzzy matching directly.

tasks.name: Adversarial and edge-case injection
tasks.detail: Support deliberate injection of: clock drift on a specific camera (sightings offset by N seconds, testing stage 09's correction); a camera outage window with zero sightings; duplicate sightings of the same pass (testing dedup); out-of-order arrival of records; a decoy vehicle with a plate identical to the target's (plate cloning); timestamps landing exactly on plausibility window boundaries.

tasks.name: Ground-truth artifact
tasks.detail: Every generated dataset emits a GroundTruth object and file containing: the true sighting_id -> vehicle_id assignment for every sighting, the true ordered trajectory per vehicle, the true plate for every vehicle, and a log of every corruption applied. Matching and pathing evaluations in later stages score against this file.

tasks.name: Determinism
tasks.detail: Generation is fully seeded. The same scenario file plus the same seed must produce byte-identical output. This is non-negotiable — it is what makes stage 6-8 tests reproducible. Provide the seed in the emitted ground truth.

tasks.name: Committed regression scenarios
tasks.detail: Author and commit at least six scenarios as fixtures: (1) 'clean' — perfect reads, no decoys; (2) 'realistic' — moderate noise, moderate traffic; (3) 'degraded' — heavy OCR noise, many failed reads, embeddings must carry the load; (4) 'hard_negatives' — decoys visually near-identical to the target; (5) 'sparse_coverage' — target passes through gaps requiring multi-hop reasoning; (6) 'adversarial' — clock drift, outage, duplicates, and a cloned plate combined.

tasks.name: CLI and loader
tasks.detail: Provide scripts/generate_dataset.py taking a scenario file, seed, and output target (JSON file or direct database load), plus a loader that seeds a repository (real or in-memory) from a generated dataset for use in tests and demos.

tests_substage.description: A buggy generator produces confidently wrong evaluations downstream, so the generator itself must be verified against its own declared ground truth.

cases: same scenario and seed produce identical output across two runs (compare full serialized output)
different seeds produce different output
seed is recorded in the ground-truth artifact and matches the requested seed
generated sightings for a route appear on exactly the specified cameras in the specified order
every consecutive pair of generated sightings satisfies is_transition_plausible against the topology (self-consistency check)
jitter stays within the configured bounds
a route revisiting a camera produces the correct number of sightings on it
a route with a skipped camera omits that camera and the remaining hops are still multi-hop plausible
timestamps are strictly increasing along a route
with corruption probability 0, every generated plate exactly equals the vehicle's true plate
with corruption probability 1, no generated plate equals the true plate
substitution corruptions only ever use characters from the configured confusion set
dropout produces a strictly shorter string
complete read failure yields plate_text None while embedding remains present
confidence is negatively correlated with corruption severity across a large sample (assert on the correlation coefficient)
every corruption applied is recorded in the ground-truth corruption log
edit distance between corrupted and true plate never exceeds the configured maximum
all generated embeddings are L2-normalized within tolerance
all embeddings have the configured dimension
mean intra-vehicle cosine similarity exceeds mean inter-vehicle similarity by a clear margin in the default config
raising intra_class_sigma measurably lowers intra-vehicle similarity
hard-negative decoys produce inter-class similarities in the configured elevated range
with hard negatives enabled, at least one decoy exceeds the naive embedding threshold — i.e. the scenario is genuinely hard
requested decoy volume is produced within tolerance
decoy routes are themselves topology-plausible
near-miss plate generation produces plates at exactly the requested edit distances from the target
no decoy accidentally shares the target's exact plate unless the cloning option is enabled
clock drift injection offsets exactly the specified camera's raw timestamps by the specified amount and records it in ground truth
outage window contains zero sightings for the affected camera
duplicate injection produces sightings with distinct ids but identical vehicle, camera, and near-identical timestamps
plate cloning produces two distinct vehicle_ids sharing one plate string in ground truth
boundary-timestamp injection produces at least one hop with elapsed exactly equal to min_travel_time and one exactly equal to max_travel_time
every generated sighting_id appears exactly once in the ground-truth assignment map
the ground-truth trajectory for each vehicle is time-ordered and contains exactly that vehicle's sightings
the number of sightings in ground truth equals the number generated (no orphans, no phantoms)
ground truth serializes to JSON and reloads to an equal object
a generated dataset loads into a real Postgres repository without constraint violations
all referenced camera_ids exist after topology sync (no FK failures)
loading the same dataset twice with conflict-ignore produces no duplicates
loaded sightings read back from the database equal the generated ones
embeddings survive the database round trip and remain L2-normalized within float32 tolerance
all six committed scenarios generate successfully without error
each scenario's generated data is self-consistent with its ground truth

each scenario's characteristics match its intent — asserted quantitatively (e.g. the 'degraded' scenario has a plate read-failure rate above a stated threshold; the 'clean' scenario has zero corruptions)
generation of the largest scenario completes within a documented time budget (marked 'slow')

exit_criteria: Generation is byte-for-byte deterministic given a scenario and seed
All six regression scenarios are committed and load cleanly into both in-memory and Postgres repositories
Every generated dataset is self-consistent with its emitted ground truth, verified by test
The noise model reproduces all five named OCR failure modes and records each occurrence
Hard-negative generation is demonstrably hard, not decorative
deliverables: docs/SYNTHETIC_DATA.md documenting the scenario format and noise model parameters
